Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

choice noun

choosing, what is chosen

also make a choice, a good choice, selection, choice of words

classical

Caesar in Cic. Brut. 253: verbōrum dīlēctum orīginem esse ēloquentiae
Cic. Off. 1.49: acceptōrum autem beneficiōrum sunt dīlēctūs habendī

dēlēctus (dīlēctus), dēlēctūs m.

noun, fourth declension

a choosing, a careful selection; discernment

Lewis & Short gives both spellings (dīlēctus in many editions, after the best manuscripts); sine dēlēctū, without discrimination. Also the levy of soldiers. Making a choice is usually the verb, ēligere (see choose).

Other words

  • ēlēctiō, ēlēctiōnis f. — a choice, a selection

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 68: jūdicium ēlēctiōque verbōrum; Quint. 1.12.4; Tac. Dial. 23 (Lewis & Short)

    Once in Cicero, then in Quintilian, Tacitus and other imperial prose (Lewis & Short); in Christian Latin the election of the faithful.

Examples

  • verbōrum dīlēctum orīginem esse ēloquentiae

    that the choice of words is the origin of eloquenceCaesar in Cic. Brut. 253

  • Acceptōrum autem beneficiōrum sunt dīlēctūs habendī

    But among favours received we must make distinctionsCic. Off. 1.49

See also choose, choice, decide.

SourcesLewis & Short: delectus · Lewis & Short: electio
